text:
Every conversation about the Penguins right now ends at the same place: is this the season the Crosby and Malkin era comes apart? The New York Times has Sidney Crosby, 39 and with his contract expiring, nearing "a crossroad." Daily Faceoff's headline reads "As struggling Penguins inch toward fire sale, what happens to Evgeni Malkin?" and Erik Karlsson's name is in every trade column. Elliotte Friedman has said, per Sportskeeda's headline, that the Penguins won't insult Malkin and Karlsson by trading them against their will.

The hockey underneath is better than a 7-10-2 record. Pittsburgh has 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five and 49% overall, and its shooters have scored about 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserved. Our numbers say the Penguins should have about four more points than they do. The power play, at 0.46 expected goals a game, has been a weak spot.

The goaltending has been the other one. Arturs Silovs has a .855 save percentage over his last five starts, 3.6 goals worse than expected, which is why Sergei Murashov's 34-save shootout win in San Jose on Wednesday mattered. The depth line of Connor Dewar, Blake Lizotte and Nick Robertson has been a quiet positive, 4-1.

Our numbers give Pittsburgh a 19% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 85 points. That number, more than any single game, is what the front office's decisions will hang on.
